title: Deep Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in the Treatment of Tinnitus
official: Deep Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in the Treatment of Tinnitus
summary:
Study of the efficacy of different H-coils in chronic tinnitus. Hypothesis: Active Deep repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation deeprTMS reduces tinnitus distress more effectively than placebo stimulation.

Randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study with three treatment arms; additional comparison with a historical rTMS control group.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Chronic tinnitus (\> 6 months)
* Moderate tinnitus burden-corresponding to a score of ≥ 18 on the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory
* Stable medication regimen with psychoactive substances

Exclusion Criteria:

* Objective tinnitus
* Severe and unstable internal medicine, neurological, and psychiatric comorbidities (particularly acute psychosis, severe depression, or substance dependence; epilepsy; brain tumor; encephalitis; history of traumatic brain injury)
* Presence of contraindications for TMS (electrical implants or metallic objects in the body, such as a pacemaker or insulin pump)
* Currently undergoing or planning to undergo tinnitus treatment during the study
* Meniere's disease, otosclerosis, acoustic neuroma, or other clear-cut or treatment-requiring causes of tinnitus
